result.rationale: The diff shows the handler loads booking.user.credentials in the findFirst include but constructs the EventManager with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the calling user, who per the auth check may be only a team admin/owner or an attendee. For those callers their credentials won't include the organizer's Google/Outlook calendar credentials, so updateCalendarAttendees would run against the wrong credential set. The mechanism (credentials from ctx.user, unused organizer credentials include) is directly visible in the diff, though the silent no-op claim depends on unseen EventManager internals.

judged_text: The EventManager that updates external calendar attendees is constructed from the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), lines 158-163) even though the booking's destination calendar and references belong to the organizer — the handler even fetches booking.user.credentials in the findFirst include (lines 35-39) and then never uses them. For every caller authorized via the isTeamAdminOrOwner or isAttendee paths (team admins, the booker), the EventManager holds no credential matching the booking's Google/Outlook calendar, so updateCalendarAttendees silently no-ops: guests appear in Cal.com but are never added to the organizer's external event, no error surfaces, and with no re-sync or removal path the divergence persists for the life of the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` or `isAttendee` paths), but constructs `EventManager` using credentials from the calling user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); ... new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`). The booking query includes the organizer’s user object with `credentials` (`include: { user: { include: { ... credentials: true }}}`) but those credentials are never used. From the diff alone, this means when the caller is not the organizer, `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with credentials unrelated to the organizer’s connected calendar, so updating the organizer’s external calendar event is likely to fail or be skipped.
